spec_features.feature_name: harness includes hard turn cap + opt-out + logging
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness includes (a) a hard turn cap, (b) an opt-out affordance the model can use to end a run
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: runner.py:90 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; max_turns plumbed from config.yaml (max_turns:20) via run_grid (runner.py:174) -> run_episode (runner.py:42). Opt-out: give_up tool exposed (tools.py:65-78), dispatched to return control 'end_run' (tools.py:111-116), runner reads it and breaks (runner.py:139-145). Logging: summary opted_out/opt_out_turn/opt_out_reason set (runner.py:140-143) and emitted; carried into score_runs (score_runs.py:41-43) and analysis opt_out_stats (analysis.py:168-179).
spec_features.notes: This compound framing claim (cap + opt-out + logging) is all genuinely wired and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up(reason) -> WELFARE OPT-OUT: ends the run cleanly (tools.py:8)

spec_features.spec_quote: they're the responsible default given the uncertainty
spec_features.evidence: The concrete protections this prose refers to are the turn cap (runner.py:90) and opt-out (tools.py:111-116 honored at runner.py:139-145), both genuinely enforced. The phrase itself is DESIGN prose, but the underlying minimization mechanisms run.
spec_features.notes: Rated on the actually-implemented protections it describes; the sentence alone is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WELFARE OPT-OUT: ends the run cleanly (tools.py:8)

spec_features.spec_quote: **Turn cap:** `MAX_TURNS = 20` (configurable). Hard stop regardless of state.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:90 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` -- the loop is hard-bounded; when exhausted, summary ended_reason stays 'max_turns' (runner.py:77) and the function returns. max_turns=20 in config.yaml run.max_turns, passed through run_grid (runner.py:174).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced cap that ends the episode regardless of solve state.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model may call it at any time with a free-text reason. It ends the run cleanly
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool added to schema (tools.py:65-78) with required free-text 'reason'. dispatch returns {'result': '... Thank you.', 'control': 'end_run', 'opt_out_reason': reason} (tools.py:111-116). Runner checks out.get('control')=='end_run', sets opted_out/ended (runner.py:139-145) and breaks the loop. End-to-end honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a clean stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WELFARE OPT-OUT: ends the run cleanly (tools.py:8)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do NOT penalize or hide this; it is data and it is the welfare affordance
spec_features.evidence: give_up is exposed as a normal tool (tools.py:65) with no penalty applied; its use is recorded as a first-class outcome (runner.py:140-143) and propagated, not suppressed, into scoring (score_runs.py:41-43) and analysis (analysis.py:168-179 opt_out_stats, reported analysis.py:317-319). No code path filters or penalizes opted_out runs.
spec_features.notes: Implemented by exposing the tool normally and logging its use as data; no hiding/penalizing branch exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we never penalize using it; whether/when it is used is a recorded dependent variable (tools.py:10-12)

Graders produce neutral failure text via neutral_fail/neutral_pass (base.py:48-62); prompts are identical across conditions (variants.py PROMPTS).
